title: Comparative Evaluation of Chia (Salvia hispanica) and Moringa (Moringa oleifera) Seeds as Green Coagulants for Sustainable Textile Wastewater Treatment
content: Background: Textile dyeing effluents in Bangladesh are characterised by high chemical oxygen demand (COD; up to 2,200 mg/L), elevated turbidity, and recalcitrant organic loadings that pose formidable challenges to wastewater treatment infrastructure. Conventional chemical coagulants carry residual toxicity, sludge-management complexity, and cost barriers for small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs).Methods: This study evaluates and directly compares the coagulation–flocculation (CF) performance of seed powders from chia (Salvia hispanica L.) and moringa (Moringa oleifera Lam.) in treating two textile dyeing effluents (initial COD: 2,100–2,200 mg/L) collected from two commercial facilities in Narayanganj, Dhaka, Bangladesh. Experiments were conducted across pH 1–10 and coagulant dosages of 0.05–1.0 g/250 mL. Key parameters—COD, dissolved oxygen (DO), and pH—were measured using APHA Standard Methods (23rd ed., 2017). One-way ANOVA was applied to compare mean COD removal between coagulant types.Results: Moringa seed (MS) coagulation achieved COD removal efficiencies of 84.76–96.19% (Effluent 1) and 20.00–96.36% (Effluent 2), with highest removal at strongly acidic (pH 1) and alkaline (pH 10) conditions. Chia seed (CS) coagulation yielded 8.57–88.57% (Effluent 1) and 23.64–96.36% (Effluent 2), demonstrating greater sensitivity to strongly acidic conditions. One-way ANOVA (nMS = 11, nCS = 22; N = 33) revealed no statistically significant difference in mean COD removal between MS (mean = 80.9%) and CS (mean = 67.8%) across pooled conditions [F(1,31) = 2.13, p = 0.155]. Mean post-treatment DO was higher following MS treatment (10.45 mg/L, Effluent 1; 9.92 mg/L, Effluent 2) compared to CS treatment (6.91 mg/L and 8.30 mg/L, respectively).Conclusions: Moringa seeds exhibit broader pH tolerance and superior post-treatment DO restoration compared to chia seeds, while both bio-coagulants achieve equivalent peak COD removal (96.36%) under optimised alkaline conditions. Neither coagulant demonstrated statistically superior mean performance across the full experimental range. Both represent environmentally sustainable, biodegradable alternatives to synthetic chemical coagulants for primary textile wastewater treatment in Bangladesh.
